messages:
Taylor Lee: Running into a parity bug between Java and Kotlin SDKs: Kotlin retry path fails when request body is non-repeatable; Java example retries fine.
Jordan Kim: interesting, are they using the same OkHttp version and interceptors order?
Taylor Lee: yep OkHttp 4.11, same interceptors. Logs show stream consumed on first attempt and subsequent retry immediately errors with EOF. Java sample buffers the body into a byte[] before making the call.
Maya Patel: that's the root cause: a streaming RequestBody is one-shot. Our Kotlin sample used a streaming wrapper to avoid OOMs, Java sample used buffered bytes. We should document that retry semantics differ unless body is repeatable.
Taylor Lee: also saw different behavior on emulator vs device: emulator tolerates a retry sometimes, device rarely. Could be timing/keepalive differences.
Jordan Kim: two action items: 1) update Kotlin sample to default to repeatable body for small payloads with BufferingRequestBody up to a threshold, 2) add clear error when retry suppressed that instructs devs to buffer or pre-auth.
QA-bot: created ticket RD-INF-7710: "sdk: non-repeatable request body -> suppressed retry; align java/kotlin samples and add docs"
Maya Patel: long-term: expose a builder option like sdk.enableBufferedRetries(maxBytes) and keep it off by default to avoid memory surprises. Add telemetry when suppressed-retry occurs.
Taylor Lee: test plan: MockWebServer closes connection mid-body in CI test to validate both buffered and non-buffered flows. I'll send a patch to samples and quickstart notes. :thumbsup:
